title: Subspaces of finite cartesian ultrametric spaces are cartesian
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space with a definite norm $N:V\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ satisfying $N(-v)=N(v)$, $N(v+w)\le\max(N(v),N(w))$ and $N(av)=|a|N(v)$. Suppose $V$ has a finite basis $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ with $$N\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i v_i\right)=\max_{1\le i\le n}|a_i|N(v_i).$$ Let $U\subseteq V$ be a $K$-linear subspace, meaning a subset containing zero and closed under addition and scalar multiplication. Then $U$ has a finite basis $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ with $$N\left(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j u_j\right)=\max_{1\le j\le m}|a_j|N(u_j).$$ An empty maximum is zero; $V=0$ and $U=0$ are allowed. No completeness or spherical completeness is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 2.3.3/4, subspace permanence for cartesian spaces; cited in Proposition 3.6.2/3, printed p.158 Local archival copy absent; WANTED in report.

proof.text: Induct on the number $n$ of vectors in the given orthogonal basis, with the claim quantified over every such normed space and every subspace. If $n=0$, then $V=U=0$ and the empty basis works. At any induction stage $U=0$ also has the empty basis. Otherwise choose $0\ne u\in U$, write $u=\sum_i c_i v_i$, and put $r_i=N(v_i)>0$. The assumed formula gives $N(u)=\max_i|c_i|r_i>0$; since this maximum is finite, choose $j$ attaining it. Thus $c_j\ne0$.

source.place: Agent coordinate-pivot proof of subspace permanence; archival BGR copy absent (WANTED). The original proposition numbering has not been verified. Step 1.

proof.text: Let $H$ be the subspace of vectors whose $j$th coordinate in the given basis is zero. The family $(v_i)_{i\ne j}$ is a basis of $H$: its expansions are exactly the expansions with $j$th coordinate zero, and uniqueness follows from uniqueness in the original basis. Its norm formula is the assumed one with the $j$th coefficient set to zero. Thus $H$, with the restricted norm, satisfies the induction hypothesis with $n-1$ basis vectors. This includes $H=0$ when $n=1$.

source.place: Agent coordinate-pivot proof of subspace permanence; archival BGR copy absent (WANTED). The original proposition numbering has not been verified. Step 2.

proof.text: For $x=\sum_i x_i v_i\in U$, the field inverse of $c_j$ exists by [def-weil-field]. Set $a=x_j/c_j$ and $w=x-au$. Closure of $U$ gives $w\in U$, and its $j$th coordinate is $x_j-ac_j=0$, so $w\in U\cap H$. This expresses every $x\in U$ as $au+w$. The expression is unique: if $au+w=a'u+w'$ with $w,w'\in H$, taking $j$th coordinates gives $(a-a')c_j=0$, hence $a=a'$ and $w=w'$.

source.place: Agent coordinate-pivot proof of subspace permanence; archival BGR copy absent (WANTED). The original proposition numbering has not been verified. Step 3.

proof.text: For any $a\in K$ and $w\in H$, put $z=au+w$. Its $j$th coordinate is $ac_j$, so the original norm formula gives $N(z)\ge|ac_j|r_j=|a|N(u)=N(au)$. Also $N(w)=N(z-au)\le\max(N(z),N(-au))\le N(z)$, using $N(-au)=N(au)$. The reverse inequality $N(z)\le\max(N(au),N(w))$ is the given ultrametric inequality. Consequently $N(au+w)=\max(|a|N(u),N(w))$. This is a direct coordinate calculation, also when $a=0$ or $w=0$.

source.place: Agent coordinate-pivot proof of subspace permanence; archival BGR copy absent (WANTED). The original proposition numbering has not been verified. Step 4.

proof.text: The intersection $U\cap H$ is a subspace of $H$, since both membership conditions are preserved by zero, addition and scalar multiplication. Apply the induction hypothesis to obtain a finite orthogonal basis $w_1,\ldots,w_t$ of $U\cap H$. The unique expression in step 3 and the unique expansion in this basis show that $(u,w_1,\ldots,w_t)$ is a basis of $U$. For arbitrary coefficients, step 4 yields $$N\left(au+\sum_k b_k w_k\right)=\max\left(|a|N(u),\max_k |b_k|N(w_k)\right).$$ This is the required formula, including $t=0$ with empty maximum zero, and completes the induction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-4ef38dd79 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and the item's five-step proof is correct. Shape: one commit containing only the item and the report, with a Q29 review section; statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there are no new nodes. Steps: step 1 sets up an induction on n that covers every normed space and subspace, and picks a pivot coordinate j where the finite maximum is attained, so c_j is nonzero. Step 2 shows the hyperplane H (j-th coordinate zero) satisfies the induction hypothesis with n-1 basis vectors. Step 3 uses def-weil-field, whose statement gives exactly the inverse of c_j it needs, and splits U uniquely as Ku plus the part of U inside H. Step 4 proves N(au+w)=max(|a|N(u),N(w)) from the j-th coordinate and the ultrametric inequality, without assuming the terms cannot cancel. Step 5 combines these. Every step is genuinely elementary, nothing assumes completeness, and the only citation is def-weil-field, so there is no cycle. Small cases tested: n=0 and U=0; Q_p^2 with U spanned by (1,p) and by (p,1); Q with the trivial absolute value and two tied coordinates, where cancellation does no harm; unequal weights, where the pivot follows |c_i|r_i. Source: Bosch-Guentzer-Remmert, Non-Archimedean Analysis, is not in literature/ and I could not read it either; the proof is correctly marked as agent-written with the book listed as wanted, and the conflicting inherited proposition numbers (2.3.3/4 here, 2.4.1/5 in the scalar-tower node) are disclosed.
